analyst_view.overall: Early view: Milan host Parma four days before Sunderland visit in the Europa League; Amorim had a long injury list before the break, so who is back by December will matter. Parma's Abdoulaye Ndiaye is listed as suspended, but his red card against Bologna was for denying a clear chance, which normally means a one-match ban, so he should have served it at Roma. Parma beat Atalanta 3-0 before the break but are 16th.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Milan's home games have averaged four goals, and Milan finish their few chances well, with Cissé and Pulisic both scoring at Genoa. Parma's games are the lowest-scoring in the league, so I would not go much higher.

corners.text: The site expects 9.1 corners. I lean lower: Milan's games have averaged under seven corners, the fewest in Serie A, and Milan win only about two corners a game at home. Parma rarely win corners themselves.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean lower because Milan's home games have averaged only about 2.6 cards, and Parma's away games about 1.6. Neither side has made a habit of fouling in these settings.

shots.text: The site expects 27.2 shots. I lean lower: Milan's home games have averaged about 21 shots, the fewest of any top side, and Parma take only about eight shots a game away. Milan take few shots and score from them.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target, close to Milan's home average of about nine. Milan shoot accurately from fewer attempts, and Parma rarely hit the target, so I stay with the number.
